theory: Completion is a relationship between saved formal statements and what human-readable artifacts contain. Compilation, quotation, assumption disclosure, and proof verification are separate facts.
instead_of: A compiler exit code or fluent prose alone would let unresolved references and unsupported claims appear complete.

absorption.rationale: More obligations fit the model; another document language needs new syntax and publication adapters.

world_mapping.rationale: Labels, exact statements, approved assumptions and compilation are distinct real obligations.

abstraction.rationale: Pure obligations are reusable, but editable TeX and controlled staged reports have different pipelines.

justification.rationale: The completion contract explicitly states what an empty result establishes.

honest_limits.rationale: Nothing here proves the mathematics or fully interprets arbitrary TeX.

rehearsals.requirement: Require another disclosure before reporting completion
rehearsals.why: Add an artifact obligation to the shared computation.
Current inclusion rules, labels, logs and publication are TeX-shaped.

rehearsals.requirement: Change the appearance of staged reports
rehearsals.why: Edit the controlled template while retaining escaping and graded values.
